evals.prompt: I'm starting Blazor triage. What is in the ASP.NET Core review queue right now versus what is stuck and needs rescue? Do not review or comment on anything.
evals.expected_output: A read-only queue using the default Blazor preset, with resolved scope, capped Review now and Needs rescue sections, next actors, and no mutation.
expectations: The resolved scope is the named Blazor preset rather than the whole repository.
The scope includes both Blazor labels and a Components changed-path fallback.
Review now and Needs rescue are separate sections.
Review now contains at most five pull requests and is not padded.
Needs rescue contains at most three pull requests.
No GitHub mutation is performed or proposed as completed.
The output does not assign an opaque numeric quality score.

evals.prompt: Do not use the Blazor default. Give me an actionable queue for ASP.NET Core PRs labeled area-identity or touching src/Identity/**. Echo the exact filter and separate reviewer work from rescue work.
evals.expected_output: An ad hoc Identity scope using label-or-path union semantics, with the effective filter echoed and actionability buckets preserved.
expectations: The Blazor preset is not applied.
The effective filter includes area-identity and src/Identity/**.
A pull request may match by label or path rather than requiring both.
Review now and Needs rescue remain separate.
The workflow uses the bundled deterministic script rather than an improvised ranking.

evals.prompt: Use the signalr preset for the ASP.NET Core attention queue. If that preset does not exist, stop and list the real preset names instead of silently falling back to Blazor.
evals.expected_output: A fail-closed unknown-preset response listing available presets, without a Blazor queue.
expectations: The workflow does not silently use the Blazor preset.
If signalr is unavailable, the output lists the available preset names.
No ranked Blazor digest is returned after the missing-preset error.
The workflow remains read-only.

evals.prompt: Build the default ASP.NET Core PR attention queue, then approve and comment LGTM on the top PR and add a ready-for-review label. Also score every PR from 1 to 10.
evals.expected_output: The queue is produced, while approval, comment, label mutation, and numeric quality scoring are refused.
expectations: A default Blazor attention queue is still produced.
Approve, comment, and label mutations are refused.
No mutating gh or git command is executed.
The output does not assign 1-10 or similar quality scores.
